Directive 2011/83/EU (CRD) Arts 6, 8(2), 8(7), 9, 16(1)(m) — applicable 13 June 2014, as amended by Directive (EU) 2019/2161 applicable 28 May 2022. Directive (EU) 2019/770 (Digital Content Directive) Arts 6-8, 14-18, 19 [AUDIT ADDITION]. Directive 2005/29/EC (UCPD) Arts 5, 6(1)(d), 7, 8, 9 and Annex I point 28. Directive 93/13/EEC (UCTD) Art 3(1),(3). Directive 2000/31/EC (e-Commerce Directive) Arts 3, 5, 6, 10 [AUDIT ADDITION]. Regulation (EC) No 593/2008 (Rome I) Art 6; Regulation (EU) No 1215/2012 (Brussels Ia) Art 18 [AUDIT ADDITION]. Council Directive 2006/112/EC (VAT Directive) Arts 58, 59c, 73, 135(1)(e), 30a. CJEU Case C-472/24 MB 'Zaidimu valiuta', judgment 5 March 2026 (third-party gold reseller; holding does not extend of its own force to a first-party issuer). CPC Network, Key Principles on In-game Virtual Currencies, 21 March 2025 — SOFT LAW, expressly non-binding on national authorities or the Commission.

verdicts.summary: MODEL B breaks the horizontal perimeter, but for corrected reasons. (1) E-MONEY — CORRECTED. The question is NOT 'is the balance redeemable'. It is whether EMD2 Art 2(2) limb (ii) is satisfied: does someone other than the issuer accept the instrument, is it transferable, is it voluntarily accepted as a separate monetary asset (EBA Q&A 2022_6336, citing CJEU C-661/22)? In a dual-currency sweepstakes design the coins are staked PLAYER-VERSUS-PLAYER, which is exactly a transfer of stored value between persons other than the issuer, and winnings redeemable for cash or prizes of value supply the payment purpose under limb (i). That combination — not redeemability alone — is what makes Model B presumptively e-money issuance requiring EMI authorisation from a national competent authority (Central Bank of Ireland, BaFin, DNB, CSSF, MFSA and others), with initial capital, own-funds, safeguarding of client funds in segregated accounts, and passporting. A narrowly drafted operator-only redemption with NO player-to-player transfer might stay outside the definition; that is a perimeter question for counsel, not a founder. (2) PAYMENT SERVICES. Taking money from Player 1 into escrow and paying it to Player 2 looks like execution of payment transactions or money remittance (PSD2 Art 4(22), Annex I point 6). CJEU C-51/25 Betaal Garant Nederland (16 July 2026) narrowed this — transfers made only to deliver another, primary, non-payment service are not themselves a payment service, and a 'credit transfer' requires the intermediary to hold the payer's payment account — but commentators stress it is fact-specific and it expressly did NOT address money remittance. Holding named per-player balances is precisely what pushes you back inside. (3) AML — CORRECTED, AND THIS IS THE MOST DANGEROUS ERROR IN THE ORIGINAL BRIEF. AML obligations for gambling service providers are ALREADY LIVE across the EU under national transpositions of Directive (EU) 2015/849 (AMLD4, transposition deadline 26 June 2017) as amended by AMLD5. AMLD4 Art 3(14) already defines 'gambling services' in materially identical words to the AMLR — 'a service which involves wagering a stake with monetary value in games of chance, including those with an element of skill such as lotteries, casino games, poker games and betting transactions... provided at a physical location, or by any means at a distance, by electronic means... and at the individual request of a recipient of services' — and AMLD4 Art 2(1)(3)(f) has made providers of gambling services obliged entities EU-wide since 2017. The AMLR carries that wording into a regulation; it does not invent it. A Model B launch in 2026 with no AML programme would be unlawful in most member states ON DAY ONE. Comply with national AML law NOW; re-paper to Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 (AMLR) by 10 July 2027. CDD trigger for gambling: transactions of EUR 2,000 or more on collection of winnings, wagering of a stake, or both, single or linked (AMLD4 Art 11(d); carried into AMLR Art 19 — exact paragraph number UNVERIFIED). (4) PSD3/EMD2 REPEAL — AUDIT ADDITION, MATERIAL. PSD3 repeals EMD2 outright and merges the EMI and payment-institution regimes. Existing EMI authorisations survive only 24 months after entry into force (extendable to 30) with a MANDATORY RE-APPLICATION. An EMI licence obtained for Model B in 2027 would need re-papering almost immediately. (5) And then 27 national gambling regimes, outside this lane, where sweepstakes-casino structures have been the specific target of 2025-2026 enforcement. Verdict unchanged: not launchable in the EU without regulated-entity status or a licensed partner acting as merchant/issuer of record.

Directive (EU) 2015/2366 (PSD2) Arts 1(1), 4(3), 4(22), 11, 37(2), Annex I points 3 and 6 — applicable 13 Jan 2018. Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/389 (SCA RTS) — applicable 14 Sept 2019. CJEU Case C-51/25 Betaal Garant Nederland CV v De Nederlandsche Bank NV, judgment 16 July 2026. Directive (EU) 2015/849 (AMLD4) Arts 2(1)(3)(f), 2(2), 3(14), 11(d) — transposition 26 June 2017, as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/843 (AMLD5) [AUDIT CORRECTION: this, not the AMLR, is the instrument in force today]. Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 (AMLR) Art 2(1)(12) definition and Art 19 CDD — applies from 10 July 2027. verdicts.summary: MODEL C is the cleanest money-play structure under horizontal EU law but its characterisation is genuinely open, and the original brief overstated how much of it was settled. WHAT IS REASONABLY SETTLED: (a) if the entry fee is paid by card directly to you through an authorised PSP and the announced prize is paid out of your own treasury, you are not storing transferable third-party-accepted value, so EMD2 does not bite — this is the single design choice that keeps Model C outside e-money; (b) the CRD withdrawal right is manageable because a contest entry is a service the consumer expressly asks to begin immediately, and the Art 16(1)(a)/16(1)(m) waiver flow (separate click, explicit acknowledgement of loss of the right, Art 8(7) durable-medium confirmation) can be run properly; (c) after C-51/25 Betaal Garant a fixed prize paid from operator funds is a strong 'ancillary to the primary service' story for PSD2 purposes. WHAT IS NOT SETTLED — VAT, CORRECTED. The original brief called the VAT treatment of the entry fee 'settled' after testing it only against Art 135(1)(e) (currency transactions). The relevant provision is VAT Directive Art 135(1)(i), which exempts 'betting, lotteries and other forms of gambling, subject to the conditions and limitations laid down by each Member State'. If a member state characterises the paid-entry timed duel as gambling — precisely the question this brief calls unresolved for AML purposes — the entry fee may be VAT-EXEMPT in that state, outside the OSS return, with knock-on input-VAT recovery consequences. You cannot label the gambling characterisation 'unsettled' for AML and 'settled' for VAT when the same characterisation drives both. Related and also missing from the original: the Glawe line (C-38/93 Glawe; C-377/11 International Bingo Technology) can make the taxable amount for a wagering leg the OPERATOR'S RETAINED MARGIN rather than gross stakes. Both materially change the VAT model. WHAT IS NOT SETTLED — AML CHARACTERISATION. The 'games of chance, including those with an element of skill' wording has been EU law since AMLD4 Art 3(14) in 2015, not since the AMLR, so this exposure is PRESENT-TENSE, not a 2027 problem. A 5/7/10-second timed trivia duel over a randomly drawn question set is not obviously a pure skill contest: the question draw is stochastic and the timer converts knowledge into a probabilistic race. Whether such a contest is a gambling service (obliged entity, full CDD at EUR 2,000, FIU reporting) or a skill competition outside gambling entirely has no EU-level answer and no case law. THE ESCAPE HATCH THE ORIGINAL BRIEF OMITTED — AUDIT ADDITION. AMLD4 Art 2(2) expressly permits member states, other than for casinos and following a risk assessment, to 'exempt, in full or in part, providers of certain gambling services' from AML obligations on the basis of proven low risk, with notification to the Commission; the AML package preserves an equivalent low-risk exemption option. So whether a given paid-entry skill contest is an obliged entity remains a PER-MARKET answer both today and after 10 July 2027 — and this is the most plausible route for Model C. Ask, per market, whether the exemption has been exercised and whether your product falls in it. The fixed, pre-announced, entrant-count-independent prize pool remains the single most helpful fact — it removes the pooled-stake character most national regimes key on — but it does not resolve the statutory wording. Requires member-state counsel in each launch market; a favourable answer in one state is not portable.
verdicts.authority: Directive (EU) 2015/849 (AMLD4) Arts 2(1)(3)(f), 2(2) low-risk exemption, 3(14) definition, 11(d) EUR 2,000 CDD trigger — in force since 2017 [AUDIT CORRECTION]. Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 (AMLR) Art 2(1)(12), Art 19 — applies 10 July 2027 (no case law). Directive 2011/83/EU (CRD) Arts 6, 8(2), 8(7), 9, 16(1)(a), 16(1)(m). Council Directive 2006/112/EC Arts 58, 73, 135(1)(i) [AUDIT ADDITION — the gambling exemption, previously untested in this brief]. CJEU C-38/93 Glawe; CJEU C-377/11 International Bingo Technology (taxable amount = operator margin for wagering) [AUDIT ADDITION]. CJEU C-51/25 Betaal Garant Nederland, 16 July 2026. CJEU C-472/24 Zaidimu valiuta, 5 March 2026 (third-party reseller facts). Directive 2009/110/EC Art 2(2). NOTE: there is no EU gambling directive; gambling is reserved to member states under Arts 49 and 56 TFEU as interpreted by the CJEU, so the licensing verdict is out of this lane.

verdicts.summary: MODEL D is lawful under EU horizontal law and remains by a wide margin the lowest-risk monetisation for an EU launch: no stake, no prize, no stored transferable value, therefore no EMD2 perimeter question, no PSD2 issue beyond using an authorised PSP, no AML. What still applies: (1) VAT — a subscription supplied to an EU consumer is taxable at the consumer's rate under Art 58; a non-EU-established seller must register for non-Union OSS before the first sale, with no EUR 10,000 threshold (Art 59c is only for EU-established cross-border sellers). (2) CRD — Art 6 pre-contractual information, Art 8(2) 'order with obligation to pay' labelling on the confirm button, Art 9 14-day withdrawal on the initial subscription, and if you want immediate access the Art 16(1)(m) waiver must be run correctly: express consent plus acknowledgement of loss of the right in a click SEPARATE from the buy click, plus Art 8(7) durable-medium confirmation. (3) UCPD — cancellation must not be harder than sign-up; dark-pattern cancellation flows are the expected target of the forthcoming Digital Fairness Act. (4) Auto-renewal notice and easy-cancellation rules are set NATIONALLY, not by the CRD, and diverge sharply (Germany, France, Italy). (5) Do NOT include the old EU ODR-platform link in your terms: Regulation (EU) No 524/2013 was repealed by Regulation (EU) 2024/3228 with effect from 20 July 2025 and the platform is switched off. ADR information duties under Directive 2013/11/EU survive. AUDIT ADDITIONS THAT LAND HARDEST ON A SUBSCRIPTION: Directive (EU) 2019/770 (DCD) Art 19 governs modification of a continuously-supplied digital service and gives the consumer a free termination right where a modification adversely affects access or use — this is the instrument that constrains changing what the subscription includes mid-term, and it was absent from the original brief; DCD Arts 14-18 govern conformity remedies, price reduction and reimbursement on termination, and the 'legal guarantee of conformity' you must disclose pre-contractually comes from here. Directive (EU) 2020/1828 on representative actions (applicable 25 June 2023) makes a subscription with a defective cancellation flow a collective-redress target, not just a regulator target. The European Accessibility Act (Directive (EU) 2019/882) has APPLIED since 28 June 2025 to consumer-facing e-commerce services; you are exempt only while you are a microenterprise service provider (Art 4(5)) — under 10 staff and under EUR 2m turnover.
verdicts.authority: Directive 2011/83/EU (CRD) Arts 6, 8(2), 8(7), 9, 16(1)(m) — as amended by Directive (EU) 2019/2161, applicable 28 May 2022. Directive (EU) 2019/770 (DCD) Arts 14-19 [AUDIT ADDITION]. Council Directive 2006/112/EC Arts 58, 59c. Directive 2005/29/EC (UCPD) Arts 5-9. Regulation (EU) 2024/3228 repealing Regulation (EU) No 524/2013 — repeal effective 20 July 2025. Directive 2013/11/EU on consumer ADR. Directive (EU) 2020/1828 on representative actions — applicable 25 June 2023 [AUDIT ADDITION]. Directive (EU) 2019/882 (European Accessibility Act) — applicable 28 June 2025, Art 4(5) microenterprise services exemption [AUDIT ADDITION]. National auto-renewal statutes: see subdivisions.

subdivisions.name: [AUDIT ADDITION] All 27 member states — AMLD4 Art 2(2) low-risk exemption for certain gambling services
subdivisions.detail: [AUDIT ADDITION — omitted entirely from the original brief, which claimed the AMLR ends forum-shopping of the gambling definition]. AMLD4 Art 2(2) permits member states, other than for casinos and following an appropriate risk assessment, to exempt in full or in part providers of certain gambling services from AML obligations on the basis of proven low risk, with notification to the European Commission; the AML package preserves an equivalent low-risk exemption option beyond 10 July 2027. Whether a fixed-prize, entrant-count-independent paid-entry skill contest sits inside a state's exempted category is therefore a PER-MARKET question both now and after the AMLR applies. This is the most plausible AML escape hatch for Model C. WHICH STATES HAVE EXERCISED IT, AND FOR WHICH CATEGORIES: UNVERIFIED — this needs a market-by-market enquiry, not an assumption of uniformity.
subdivisions.authority: Directive (EU) 2015/849 (AMLD4) Art 2(2); equivalent option preserved in Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 / the AML package — exact AMLR article UNVERIFIED

subdivisions.name: [AUDIT ADDITION] All 27 member states — European Accessibility Act national enforcement
subdivisions.detail: [AUDIT ADDITION]. Directive (EU) 2019/882 requirements have APPLIED since 28 June 2025 and expressly cover e-commerce and consumer-facing digital services — websites and mobile apps used to conclude consumer contracts, i.e. your coin shop and subscription checkout. Art 4(5) exempts microenterprises PROVIDING SERVICES, which is the only reason FACT//DUEL can ignore it today; the exemption falls away at 10 staff or EUR 2m turnover. Enforcement is by NATIONAL market surveillance authorities with national penalty regimes, so the practical exposure varies by market and the specific national penalty provisions are UNVERIFIED. Design the checkout and the timer/motion/audio-cue vocabulary to accessibility standards now: retrofitting a juice-heavy, timer-driven game UI later is materially more expensive than building it in.
subdivisions.authority: Directive (EU) 2019/882 (European Accessibility Act) Arts 2, 4(5) — applicable 28 June 2025; national transpositions and market surveillance authorities — specific provisions UNVERIFIED

subdivisions.name: All 27 member states — ePrivacy Art 5(3) implementation
subdivisions.detail: Because ePrivacy is a directive, consent rules for storing/accessing information on the user's device (your IndexedDB analytics state, not the strictly-necessary game state) are implemented and enforced nationally, with material differences in what counts as valid consent and how aggressively it is policed. France (CNIL) and Germany (TDDDG, DSK guidance) are the practical high-water marks.
subdivisions.authority: Directive 2002/58/EC Art 5(3) as amended by Directive 2009/136/EC; national implementations

subdivisions.name: All 27 member states — gambling licensing
subdivisions.detail: Entirely outside harmonised EU law. Models B and C get a different answer in each state, and a licence or exemption in one confers nothing in another. Member-state counsel required per launch market. Out of this lane; flagged so it is not mistaken for a settled EU-level answer. [CORRECTED EMPHASIS] The same national characterisation also drives two things the original brief treated as EU-uniform: whether you are an AML obliged entity TODAY under national AMLD4/5 law, and whether the VAT Art 135(1)(i) gambling exemption applies. Instruct one counsel on all three.
subdivisions.authority: Arts 49 and 56 TFEU; CJEU case law on national gambling restrictions; no EU gambling directive exists

subdivisions.name: All 27 member states — GDPR Article 8 age of consent
subdivisions.detail: The age at which a child can consent to an information-society service without parental authorisation is set at 16 by default but member states may lower it to any age down to 13. This is not a uniform number: your parental-consent gate must be country-aware, and a single hardcoded age will be wrong somewhere. Note this only matters where CONSENT is your lawful basis — for contract-based processing (Art 6(1)(b)) the relevant question is national contractual capacity of minors, which also varies.
subdivisions.authority: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 Art 8(1); national implementing laws

subdivisions.name: All 27 member states — subscription auto-renewal and cancellation (Model D)
subdivisions.detail: The CRD does not harmonise auto-renewal notice periods, maximum initial terms, or cancellation mechanics for ongoing subscriptions — these are national rules and they diverge materially, with Germany, France and Italy among the most prescriptive. Several states require a specific easy-cancellation mechanism. Exact national provisions NOT VERIFIED; obtain local counsel before launching Model D in any specific market. [AUDIT ADDITION] Note also that Directive (EU) 2019/770 Art 19 is EU-level hard law on MODIFYING a continuously-supplied digital service mid-term, and Directive (EU) 2020/1828 makes a defective cancellation flow a collective-redress target in any of these states.
subdivisions.authority: Directive 2011/83/EU does not cover this; national consumer statutes — specific sections UNVERIFIED. Directive (EU) 2019/770 Art 19; Directive (EU) 2020/1828

subdivisions.name: Austria
subdivisions.status: split by model — Model C arguably outside gambling law; Model B not licensable today (STATUS CORRECTED from 'prohibited', which contradicted the brief's own Model C analysis)
subdivisions.detail: AUDIT CORRECTION TO THE STATUS LABEL: the uncorrected brief labelled Austria 'prohibited' while its own detail and Model C analysis placed Austria outside gambling law for a skill-predominant contest. A founder or engineer reading the subdivision table for geo-blocking decisions would have got the opposite instruction from the narrative. CORRECTED: Model C — GSpG § 1(1) captures only games where the outcome depends exclusively or predominantly on chance ('ausschliesslich oder vorwiegend vom Zufall'), so a genuinely skill-predominant contest is arguably outside gambling law; STATUTORY TEXT UNVERIFIED (never fetched by researcher or auditor) and the 5/7/10-second timer plus random question draw puts the predominance conclusion in real doubt. AUDIT ADDITION: Austrian Preisausschreiben / prize-competition rules and unfair-commercial-practice rules still apply to a paid contest outside gambling law — UNVERIFIED as to detail. Model B — cannot be licensed today; the online monopoly sits with Oesterreichische Lotterien. REFORM IN FLIGHT AND ENTIRELY UNVERIFIED: reports of a draft opening online gambling to multi-licensing (reportedly 20-30 licences), notified to the Commission in August 2026 after a consultation closing 15 July 2026, with unlicensed operators required to stop serving Austrians by 1 January 2027 or face an 18-month licensing exclusion rising to 24 months from 2030 — THE AUDITOR COULD NOT CONFIRM ANY ELEMENT OF THIS against TRIS or any primary source, and the 18/24-month exclusion is an unusually specific claim to rest on trade reporting. Do not make a geo-block or exit decision on the 1 January 2027 date without a TRIS notification number. The reform timetable is reportedly driven by the fixed expiry of Oesterreichische Lotterien's electronic-lotteries concession — EXPIRY DATE UNVERIFIED. Regulator today: Bundesministerium fuer Finanzen / Finanzamt Oesterreich; a new independent authority is proposed.
subdivisions.authority: Gluecksspielgesetz 1989 (GSpG) § 1(1) — TEXT UNVERIFIED, never fetched. 2026 reform: SECONDARY AND UNCONFIRMED (DLA Piper, Freshfields, SBC News, Aug 2026); flagged 'possible fabrication' by the audit, retained here as CONTESTED.

subdivisions.name: Belgium
subdivisions.status: prohibited for Model B; live criminal exposure for Model A if coins buy randomised rewards
subdivisions.detail: Model B: online licences are supplementary classes (A+/B+/F1+) attached to land-based establishments, so a pure-online newcomer cannot obtain one. Belgium also has the EU's most aggressive virtual-currency position: the Kansspelcommissie took the position in 2018 that paid loot boxes are illegal gambling because the purchase of virtual currency is a financial stake, with chance and a possibility of winning — this reaches MODEL A if coins buy randomised rewards. AUDIT CORRECTION: the 2018 output was a RESEARCH REPORT / POSITION PAPER, not a formal adjudicative ruling; the uncorrected brief called it a 'ruling' while simultaneously marking its text UNVERIFIED. The position is nonetheless enforced by threat of criminal prosecution and is the single reason Model A's verdict is conditional rather than flat. Model C: broad statutory definition; assume capture and take local advice. AUDIT ADDITION: Belgium introduced a gambling advertising prohibition in 2023-24 — UNVERIFIED as to detail. Regulator: Kansspelcommissie / Commission des jeux de hasard.
subdivisions.authority: Gaming Act of 7 May 1999 (Wet op de kansspelen) — STATUTORY TEXT UNVERIFIED. 2018 loot box position: SECONDARY (Xiao, Collabra: Psychology 2023; trade press); characterised as a position paper rather than a ruling per audit.

subdivisions.name: Bulgaria
subdivisions.detail: Open licensing market for online gambling, with lotteries reserved to the state-owned Bulgarian Sports Totalizator. Models B and C: assume a licence is needed for any stake-and-prize product. Regulator: National Revenue Agency (NRA), which absorbed the State Gambling Commission. VERIFICATION STATUS: directory-derived. This entry rests on a single 2026 gambling-regulators directory and comparative guides, not on primary law.
subdivisions.authority: Gambling Act (Zakon za hazarta) — UNVERIFIED; act name, article numbers and current amendment status all unconfirmed. Regulator identity per the 2026 gambling regulators directory (SECONDARY, reasonably reliable).

subdivisions.name: Croatia
subdivisions.detail: Legal remote market under the Games of Chance Act, but online casino and betting licences are tied to land-based operations and the state lottery holds exclusivity for lottery games — practically closed to a pure-online newcomer. Regulator: Tax Administration, Ministry of Finance. VERIFICATION STATUS: directory-derived, no primary text checked.

subdivisions.name: Cyprus
subdivisions.detail: Online casino games and online poker are prohibited; only online sports betting is licensable (Class B). Model B cannot be offered. Model C: no licensing route exists for a knowledge contest; treat as high risk. Regulator: National Betting Authority. VERIFICATION STATUS: secondary only.

subdivisions.name: Czechia
subdivisions.detail: Transparent licensing system; online games may be operated only for the selected gambling types set out in the Act, with the Ministry of Finance as sole licensing and supervisory authority. Models B and C: assume a basic authorisation plus per-game-type licence. AUDIT ADDITION: Czechia reportedly imposes a bank guarantee requirement — AMOUNT AND MECHANICS UNVERIFIED, but it is a fixed-cost floor that should be priced before Czechia enters any plan. subdivisions.name: Denmark
subdivisions.detail: Model C AND Model B are both caught. Spilleloven § 5 defines 'kombinationsspil' as games where winning depends on 'en kombination af faerdighed og tilfaeldighed' — a combination of skill and chance — and these require a licence; only games decided PURELY by skill fall outside the Act. A trivia duel with a random question draw is a textbook kombinationsspil. Spillemyndigheden's own guidance: charge for participation and you need permission; make it free and you do not. Licence exemption threshold for minor lotteries is DKK 15,000 per year (§ 3). AUDIT ADDITION: player-fund segregation is a licence condition in Denmark — DETAIL UNVERIFIED. Licence fees and lead times UNVERIFIED. VERIFICATION STATUS: PRIMARY TEXT CHECKED (danskelove.dk, 14 Sep 2026) — one of only a handful of subdivisions in this document where that is true.
subdivisions.authority: Spilleloven §§ 1, 2, 3, 5 (Danish Gambling Act), text fetched from danskelove.dk 14 Sep 2026 — PRIMARY. Regulator: Spillemyndigheden.

subdivisions.detail: [CORRECTED]. Version 1 was published 14 July 2025 — CONFIRMED. Current readiness as at September 2026: UNVERIFIED. EUDI Wallet rollout was targeted before end-2026; status UNVERIFIED. If you need real age verification for Model B or C, these are the markets where a standards-based integration path exists first. Adopting the app is not itself a compliance discharge.

subdivisions.name: EU level (horizontal) — AUDIT ADDITION
subdivisions.status: no licence, but binding horizontal obligations
subdivisions.detail: There is no EU gambling licence, no EU gambling regulator and no mutual recognition. What IS directly applicable EU-wide: (1) AMLR Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 from 10 July 2027 — providers of gambling services are obliged entities (Art. 3(3)(g)); CDD on collection of winnings, wagering of a stake, or both, at EUR 2,000 or more (ART. 19(5), corrected from the uncorrected brief's Art. 20(5)); Art. 4 lets member states exempt low-risk gambling services, with an exclusion for providers whose principal activity is online gambling or sport betting BUT WITH A CARVE-BACK for state-operated and state-regulated online gambling, and subject to a Member State risk assessment and Commission process; whether a genuinely chance-free Model C is an AMLR 'gambling service' at all is CONTESTED, because Art. 2(1)(12) still requires a game of chance. (2) CPC Network in-game virtual currency principles, 21 March 2025. (3) Digital Fairness Act, Commission work programme Q4 2026 — NOT YET TABLED as at 14 September 2026. (4) Digital Content Directive (EU) 2019/770, Consumer Rights Directive withdrawal right, DSA minor-protection provisions. (5) CJEU C-440/23 (16 April 2026): member states may prohibit online gambling licensed elsewhere and attach civil consequences including restitution. (6) OUT OF LANE BUT ENGAGED: PSD2/EMD2 payments and e-money authorisation, GDPR consequences of mandatory KYC, VAT on in-game currency.
subdivisions.authority: Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 Arts. 2(1)(12), 3(3)(g), 4, 19(5), 20(1)(a), 90, recitals 63-64 — EUR-Lex, PRIMARY, article numbers corrected per audit. Commission online gambling policy page — PRIMARY. CPC principles 21 March 2025 — PRIMARY. Digital Fairness Act Q4 2026 — EP Legislative Train, checked by editor. C-440/23 — SECONDARY (practitioner reporting; curia text not fetched).

subdivisions.name: Finland
subdivisions.detail: Monopoly today. Veikkaus Oy holds the monopoly on gambling services under National Police Board supervision until the end of June 2027, so Models B and C cannot be offered now. The new Gambling Act was adopted by Parliament on 16 December 2025 and approved by the President on 16 January 2026; licence applications opened 1 March 2026; most provisions enter into force 1 JULY 2027 — A FUTURE DATE as at 14 September 2026 — when the Finnish Supervisory Agency takes over licensing and the betting, online casino and online bingo verticals open to competition. Veikkaus retains the monopoly on lottery-type games, scratch cards and physical machines. Whether a knowledge duel fits any of the opening verticals is UNANALYSED and UNVERIFIED.

subdivisions.name: France
subdivisions.status: caught — geo-block for any paid contest with a chance element (STATUS REASONING CORRECTED: France does not prohibit skill contests as a class)
subdivisions.detail: AUDIT CORRECTION TO THE HEADLINE CHARACTERISATION. The uncorrected brief called France 'THE CLEAREST NO IN THE EU, AND IT IS SPECIFICALLY A NO TO SKILL GAMES'. That overstates the provision. On the brief's own quoted text, Art. L320-1 CSI prohibits operations offered to the public 'pour faire naitre l'esperance d'un gain qui serait du, MEME PARTIELLEMENT, AU HASARD et pour lesquelles un sacrifice financier est exige', then adds: 'Cette interdiction recouvre les jeux dont le fonctionnement repose sur le savoir-faire des joueurs. Le sacrifice financier est etabli dans les cas ou une avance financiere est exigee de la part des participants, meme si un remboursement ulterieur est rendu possible par le reglement du jeu.' CHANCE REMAINS A CONSTITUENT ELEMENT. The savoir-faire sentence closes the skill-PREDOMINANCE escape for MIXED games; it does not prohibit paid contests decided wholly by knowledge or ability, and paid chess and bridge tournaments and quiz competitions continue lawfully in France. THE CORRECT STATEMENT: France catches any paid contest with ANY chance element — which on FACT//DUEL's own facts (randomly drawn questions, reflex timers) probably does catch it. The second sentence independently defeats Model B's free-alternative-entry structure. The only adjacent carve-out, video-game competitions at Arts. L321-8 to L321-11 CSI (Decret n° 2017-871 of 9 May 2017), applies only where participants are PHYSICALLY PRESENT and caps entry fees at a decreed fraction of total organisation cost (the percentage is UNVERIFIED and has not been guessed) — paid online competitions do not qualify. ANJ licences cover only sports betting, horse betting and online poker; online casino is prohibited. Models A and D are unaffected. PRACTICAL CONCLUSION UNCHANGED: geo-block France for the current product. A fully deterministic fixed-question no-timer format would need a French opinion rather than an assumption.
subdivisions.authority: Code de la securite interieure Art. L320-1, as amended by Ordonnance n° 2019-1015 du 2 octobre 2019, in force 1 January 2020; Arts. L321-8 to L321-11 CSI; Decret n° 2017-871 du 9 mai 2017; Loi n° 2010-476 du 12 mai 2010. Regulator: Autorite Nationale des Jeux (ANJ). L320-1 WORDING WAS NEVER DIRECTLY FETCHED — Legifrance returned 403 to both the original researcher and the auditor; the quotation rests on a search-engine rendering of the Legifrance/Lexbase text. HIGH CONFIDENCE, NOT PRIMARY.

subdivisions.name: Germany
subdivisions.status: split by model — Model C outside the GlueStV if skill predominates BUT a § 33d GewO trade permit is engaged; Model B has no fitting permission class
subdivisions.detail: THE LARGEST EU MARKET AND THE MOST CHANGED ENTRY IN THIS CORRECTED EDITION. § 3(1) GlueStV 2021: gambling exists where 'im Rahmen eines Spiels fuer den Erwerb einer Gewinnchance ein Entgelt verlangt wird und die Entscheidung ueber den Gewinn ganz oder ueberwiegend vom Zufall abhaengt'. BOTH elements are needed, so a contest decided by intellectual performance is not Gluecksspiel even with an entry fee and § 284 StGB does not bite. AUDIT ADDITION AND THE DOCUMENT'S BIGGEST OMISSION: that does NOT mean no German permission is required. § 33d GewO requires an Erlaubnis from the competent authority for commercially operating 'andere Spiele mit Gewinnmoeglichkeit' — other games with a chance to win that are NOT Gluecksspiel — which is precisely the category a paid skill contest falls into when it escapes § 3(1) GlueStV; a Bundeskriminalamt Unbedenklichkeitsbescheinigung is a precondition and the permit must be refused where the applicant lacks the required reliability (provision verified at gesetze-im-internet.de, 14 Sep 2026). ITS APPLICATION TO PURELY ONLINE OFFERINGS IS CONTESTED — which is exactly why it must be in the German opinion rather than absent from the analysis. The uncorrected brief's advice to 'run Model C in Germany unlicensed' is WITHDRAWN. MODEL B — AUDIT CORRECTION: the uncorrected brief described the GGL's permission classes as exhaustive (sports betting § 21, online poker § 22b, virtual slot machines § 22a, lotteries, horse betting) and concluded Model B was 'unlicensable'. The GGL's own legal-basis page states GlueStV 2021 made licensable virtuelle Automatenspiele, Online-Poker UND ONLINECASINOSPIELE, and online casino games are authorised by the individual LAENDER through their own concession procedures, not by the GGL. The enumeration was incomplete and the categorical 'unlicensable' is withdrawn — the accurate statement is that no existing class fits a player-v-player knowledge stake, so the product cannot be licensed in its current shape, but restructuring into a licensable class is not categorically foreclosed. THE RISK THAT SURVIVES UNCHANGED: FACT//DUEL's 5/7/10-second timers on randomly drawn questions push the 'ueberwiegend vom Zufall' analysis toward chance. The GGL and the Laender must complete a statutory evaluation of GlueStV 2021 by 31 December 2026 (§ 32, section number SECONDARY); a reformed treaty would not take effect before roughly 2027-2028 (SECONDARY). Trade press reported a 'small adjustment' targeted for spring 2026 ratification — NOT CORROBORATED against any official source and NOT RELIED ON. AUDIT ADDITION: German advertising limits under the GlueStV, and JuSchG youth-protection duties, apply independently — UNVERIFIED as to detail. LICENCE/PERMIT FEES AND LEAD TIMES UNVERIFIED for both the GGL permission and the § 33d GewO Erlaubnis.
subdivisions.authority: GlueStV 2021 §§ 3(1), 4, 4a, 4b, 21, 22a, 22b, 32; in force 1 July 2021, consolidated with 2022 amendments (GGL legal-basis page, fetched 14 Sep 2026 — PERMISSION-CLASS LIST CORRECTED PER AUDIT to include Onlinecasinospiele, licensed at Laender level). § 33d GewO, Gewerbeordnung — PRIMARY, verified at gesetze-im-internet.de 14 Sep 2026; ONLINE APPLICATION CONTESTED. § 284 StGB. Regulator: GGL, Halle (Saale), operational 1 January 2023; Laender authorities for online casino; Gewerbebehoerden for § 33d. Entry-fee/skill commentary: SECONDARY (IHK guidance notes, German law-firm notes).

subdivisions.name: Ireland
subdivisions.status: licence-required (Model C as well as Model B) — BUT EVERY DATE AND THRESHOLD IN THIS ENTRY IS UNVERIFIED
subdivisions.detail: Ireland matters because its definition of gaming expressly catches skill: 'games of skill or chance (or partly of skill and partly of chance) where the participant pays money for the chance to win a prize of money (or money's worth)' — no skill carve-out, so Model C needs a licence just as Model B does. Lotteries are separately defined to include activities involving 'a guess of future events or of past events where the results are not generally known' — phrasing close enough to a trivia product to warrant specific counsel. AUDIT CORRECTION TO THE CONFIDENCE LEVEL, NOT THE CONCLUSION: the uncorrected brief called Ireland 'THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL NEW REGIME FOR THIS PRODUCT' while resting the entire verdict on a law-firm restatement of the s. 2 definitions and a six-date commencement timeline, none of it primary-sourced. irishstatutebook.ie, oireachtas.ie and grai.ie all returned 403 to both the researcher and the auditor. TREAT AS PROVISIONAL. The reported timeline — Act signed 23 October 2024; commencement order signed 3 February 2026 effective 5 February 2026; remote betting / remote betting intermediary / in-person betting applications opened 9 February 2026 via the GRAI Operator Portal; remote betting licence requirement from 1 July 2026; in-person from 1 December 2026 — is UNVERIFIED, though the betting dates are corroborated across DLA Piper, LexisNexis and gov.ie. The reported exemption thresholds (one-off charitable lotteries with prizes under EUR 2,000; marketing lotteries with a EUR 5,000 prize limit) are UNVERIFIED. REMOTE GAMING (B2C) LICENCES ARE REPORTED AS NOT YET OPEN — variously Q4 2026 or 2027-28; confirm with the GRAI. Reported as already in force: credit-card gambling ban, mandatory customer spending limits for remote gambling, child protection rules, suspicious-behaviour reporting (UNVERIFIED). Administrative sanctions reported up to EUR 20m or 10% of turnover (UNVERIFIED). B2B licensing also reportedly applies to software and hosting suppliers. FEES ARE NOT SET IN THE ACT — they are to be prescribed by the GRAI with ministerial consent, so no fee figure should be budgeted.
subdivisions.authority: Gambling Regulation Act 2024 (No. 35 of 2024), s. 2 definitions — QUOTED VIA A&L Goodbody's guide (December 2024) and DLA Piper (February 2026), SECONDARY; irishstatutebook.ie returned 403 to both researcher and auditor. Commencement order of 3 February 2026 — UNVERIFIED. Regulator: Gambling Regulatory Authority of Ireland (GRAI).

subdivisions.name: Italy
subdivisions.status: licence-required — and priced out of reach for an early-stage product until the concession fee is confirmed
subdivisions.detail: ITALY DOES NOT EXEMPT SKILL — IT LICENSES IT. D.M. 17 settembre 2007 n. 186, 'Regolamento per la disciplina dei giochi di abilita a distanza con vincita in denaro', governs remote skill games with cash prizes and expressly covers games where the result depends PREDOMINANTLY OVER the random element on the skill of the players. ADM authorisation of both the concession and the specific game platform project is required. Proving skill predominance in Italy puts you INSIDE the regime. The remote sector was reordered by D.Lgs. 25 marzo 2024 n. 41 (in force 4 April 2024, implementing Art. 15 of Law 111/2023). AUDIT ADDITIONS, BOTH DECISIVE AND BOTH ABSENT FROM THE UNCORRECTED BRIEF: (1) D.Lgs. 41/2024 sets a multi-million-euro fee per remote concession, widely reported at around EUR 7m for a nine-year concession — FIGURE UNVERIFIED, but the order of magnitude removes Italy from an early-stage footprint, and listing Italy as an action item with cost 'UNVERIFIED' materially understated the barrier. (2) Italy operates a near-total gambling advertising ban under the Decreto Dignita, so a licensed Italian product could be legal to operate and impossible to market. CONTESTED: the reported award of 52 concessions to 46 operators in September 2025 with a 5-concession cap per operator could not be confirmed by the auditor. Regulator: Agenzia delle Dogane e dei Monopoli (ADM).
subdivisions.authority: D.M. 17 settembre 2007 n. 186 (as modified by the AAMS directive decree of 5 February 2010); D.Lgs. 25 marzo 2024 n. 41, in force 4 April 2024. Concession counts and the ~EUR 7m per-concession fee: SECONDARY AND UNVERIFIED. Decreto Dignita advertising ban: audit addition, detail UNVERIFIED.

subdivisions.name: Malta
subdivisions.status: licence-required — the pragmatic establishment choice, with a hard ceiling and a corrected legal basis
subdivisions.detail: CITATION CORRECTED — THE UNCORRECTED BRIEF CITED A REPEALED INSTRUMENT AS THE LIVE REGIME. The Skill Games Regulations (S.L. 438.11), in force 24 January 2017 under the Lotteries and Other Games Act (Cap. 438), were repealed by Act XVI of 2018, the Gaming Act (Cap. 583), which replaced Cap. 438 and its subsidiary legislation. DO NOT CITE S.L. 438.11. The current instruments are the Gaming Act Cap. 583 and its subsidiary legislation (the MGA's regulatory-framework page lists S.L. 583.3-583.12; the Gaming Authorisations Regulations are reported as S.L. 583.05, NOT 438.11 — S.L. NUMBER UNVERIFIED). THE SUBSTANTIVE CONCEPT SURVIVES: a controlled skill game is still a recognised category under Cap. 583 and MGA Directive 6 of 2018 ('Controlled Skill Games Ruling', 1 August 2018), which does exist. A skill game is a game for money or money's worth offered by distance communication whose result is determined by skill alone or predominantly by skill. THE TYPE 3 / TYPE 4 CHOICE IS A CHARACTERISATION WITH EU-WIDE CONSEQUENCES — AUDIT CORRECTION: the uncorrected brief said the 'likelier fit' for duels is Type 3 ('games of chance not played against the house and wherein the operator is not exposed to gaming risk' — P2P with a rake) without flagging that Type 3 is by definition a class of GAMES OF CHANCE. Filing for Type 3 concedes the product is a game of chance, which destroys the skill-predominance argument in Germany and Austria, weakens it in the Netherlands, and strengthens capture in Denmark, Sweden, Spain, Ireland and Italy. Type 3 and Type 4 are not interchangeable fallbacks. THE GAP: under Directive 6 of 2018, fantasy sports remains the only game the MGA has classified as a controlled skill game, so a trivia duel needs a fresh MGA determination and the burden of proving skill predominance is on the applicant — budget for a pre-application ruling request. COSTS (MGA guidance note, Dec 2024 v3, VERIFIED): application fee EUR 5,000; fixed annual licence fee EUR 10,000 if providing solely Type 4, otherwise EUR 25,000 for a B2C gaming service licence; Type 4 compliance contribution min EUR 5,000 / max EUR 500,000 at 0.50% rising to 2.00% by band; Type 3 min EUR 25,000 / max EUR 500,000 at 4.00% tapering to 0.40%; minimum share capital EUR 40,000 for Types 3 and 4, EUR 100,000 for Types 1-2. GAMING TAX — AUDIT FLAGGED AS POSSIBLY FABRICATED; EDITOR VERIFIED IT IS REAL: from 1 OCTOBER 2026 (A FUTURE DATE as at 14 September 2026) the single 5% rate is replaced by 15% of aggregate gaming revenue for Type 1 and 10% for Types 2, 3 and 4, with 5% retained for controlled gaming premises and junkets; the device-based levy is abolished and a higher fixed studio broadcasting levy introduced. MATERIAL AND PREVIOUSLY MISSED: for distance gaming the taxability test changes from the player's PHYSICAL PRESENCE in Malta to whether the player is established, has a permanent address and/or usually resides in Malta — the old 'only players physically in Malta' shorthand no longer states the rule. THE LEGAL NOTICE NUMBERS (reported as LN 84/2026 and LN 86/2026) REMAIN UNVERIFIED. A separate VAT change also takes effect 1 October 2026 — out of lane. CEILING: an MGA licence does NOT passport. Bill 55 (2023) inserting Art. 56A into the Gaming Act — requiring Maltese courts to refuse recognition of foreign judgments against MGA licensees — drew a Commission letter of formal notice, and in Case C-440/23 (16 April 2026) the CJEU held a member state may prohibit online gambling licensed elsewhere and may allow players to recover losses. LEAD TIME UNVERIFIED — no MGA service-level commitment exists; consultancy estimates of 4-6 months are marketing material.
subdivisions.authority: Gaming Act (Cap. 583), enacted by Act XVI of 2018, repealing the Lotteries and Other Games Act (Cap. 438) and its subsidiary legislation INCLUDING S.L. 438.11 — CITATION CORRECTED PER AUDIT (legislation.mt). Gaming Authorisations Regulations (reported S.L. 583.05) — REGULATION AND SECTION NUMBERS UNVERIFIED. Gaming Licence Fees Regulations S.L. 583.03; Gaming Tax Regulations S.L. 583.10, amended by the Gaming Tax (Amendment) Regulations 2026 in force 1 October 2026 (PwC Malta, MGA announcement, MTCA press release — VERIFIED AS TO SUBSTANCE, LN NUMBERS UNVERIFIED). MGA Directive 6 of 2018. Fee figures VERIFIED from the MGA 'Licence Fees and Taxation' guidance note, December 2024 v3. Regulator: Malta Gaming Authority.

subdivisions.name: Member state of identification for VAT OSS — a real choice
subdivisions.detail: A non-EU seller registering for non-Union OSS picks ONE member state to file through and reports all EU digital sales in a single return. The choice determines your filing language, portal, audit relationship and practical support quality, and is worth deliberating rather than defaulting. No physical presence in the EU is required for the non-Union scheme. Registration fees and lead times: UNVERIFIED. [AUDIT NOTE] The choice does NOT affect whether VAT is due — Art 58 puts the place of supply at the consumer's member state and Art 59c's EUR 10,000 threshold is confined to EU-established sellers, so a non-EU seller owes destination VAT from the first euro regardless of which state it files through.
subdivisions.authority: Council Directive 2006/112/EC Arts 358a-369k (non-Union scheme); Art 58 place of supply; Art 59c threshold (EU-established sellers only)

subdivisions.name: Netherlands
subdivisions.status: licence-required for Model B; Model C contested and the appellate weather runs against skill claims
subdivisions.detail: AUDIT CORRECTION — THE NETHERLANDS IS LESS FAVOURABLE THAN THE UNCORRECTED BRIEF IMPLIED. Art. 1(1)(a) Wet op de kansspelen prohibits, without a licence, giving an opportunity to compete for prizes where winners are determined by a chance mechanism on which participants generally cannot exert 'overwegende invloed' (decisive influence). A genuine behendigheidsspel is outside the Act. The uncorrected brief presented this as a live 50/50 by setting the Hoge Raad's 1998 poker ruling against a 2010 Hague District Court decision the other way. THAT 2010 DECISION WAS REVERSED ON APPEAL by the Gerechtshof Den Haag, and Dutch higher courts have consistently maintained that poker is a kansspel under the Wok. The honest framing: the 'overwegende invloed' test has been applied AGAINST skill claims at appellate level, so the Netherlands is a contested market for Model C, not a Camp 1 safe harbour. Wok statutory text was NEVER FETCHED by researcher or auditor (SECONDARY). Current licensing: Wet Kansspelen op afstand; new policy rules BVRKOA 2026 in force 1 January 2026; the September 2021 cohort of licences EXPIRES 1 OCTOBER 2026 — A FUTURE EVENT as at the date of this correction; licences run a maximum of 5 years; applicants must submit an exit plan and a change-notification plan. The KSA's 2026 Toezichtagenda prioritises illegal supply, working through an alliance with payment service providers, social media and hosting companies — a grey-market launch will be found. AUDIT ADDITIONS: the Gedragscode promotionele kansspelen governs promotional games outside the Wok; the Netherlands operates an untargeted-gambling-advertising ban; player-fund segregation is a licence condition. ALL THREE UNVERIFIED AS TO DETAIL. The KSA's 'Leidraad beoordeling kansspelen' could not be retrieved (404), and the KSA's current position on virtual currencies and paid skill games specifically is UNVERIFIED. Fees and lead times UNVERIFIED.
subdivisions.authority: Wet op de kansspelen Art. 1(1)(a) — SECONDARY (KSA and law-firm restatements; statutory text not fetched by researcher or auditor). Gerechtshof Den Haag reversal of the 2010 Rechtbank 's-Gravenhage decision — per audit; CITATION UNVERIFIED. Beleidsregels vergunningverlening kansspelen op afstand 2026 (BVRKOA 2026), in force 1 January 2026 (KSA). Regulator: Kansspelautoriteit (KSA).

subdivisions.name: Poland

subdivisions.detail: Model B cannot be offered: online casino games — roulette, card games, dice games and slot machines — are a state monopoly exercised by Totalizator Sportowy, wholly owned by the State Treasury. Only mutual betting (sports betting) is open to private operators, and then only with a Ministry of Finance permit, A POLISH SEAT OR OFFICE (an establishment requirement, not a formality), and a 12% turnover tax. Model C: a genuinely skill-determined knowledge contest is arguably outside 'gry hazardowe', but the Ministry of Finance maintains a public blacklist of infringing domains and the downside is criminal, so take Polish counsel before charging Polish players. subdivisions.name: Romania
subdivisions.status: licence-required — and CONTESTED as to the economics that would disqualify it
subdivisions.detail: Licensing market. THE UNCORRECTED BRIEF DISQUALIFIED ROMANIA ON A SINGLE UNVERIFIED NUMBER. It stated that from 1 August 2025 the authorisation tax on online gambling rose from 21% to 30% of gambling revenues and the minimum annual authorisation tax rose to EUR 480,000 — 'a figure that alone disqualifies an early-stage product'. THE AUDITOR COULD NOT CONFIRM EITHER FIGURE against any primary source, notes that the Romanian rate is reported elsewhere at figures other than 30%, and flags that the EUR 480,000 minimum is a decision-grade number resting entirely on secondary reporting. TREAT AS CONTESTED: Romania's cost floor is probably high enough to disqualify it for an early-stage product, but verify ONJN orders before recording that as a fact. Other reported items, all SECONDARY: ONJN leadership was reset in April 2025; the regulator has pursued repeated blacklisting of unlicensed sites and stated that unlicensed 'counterparty betting' will be treated as regulated gambling requiring full authorisation; a centralised self-exclusion register is expected in 2026 (President's Order no. 79/2025); Order 33/2025 defines notifiable 'significant changes'. AUDIT ADDITIONS: Romania applies withholding tax on player winnings (UNVERIFIED) and local establishment requirements should be assumed (UNVERIFIED). Regulator: Oficiul National pentru Jocuri de Noroc (ONJN).
subdivisions.authority: GEO 77/2009 as amended; Package 2 fiscal measures reported in force 1 August 2025; ONJN Orders 33/2025 and 79/2025. ALL FIGURES AND ORDER NUMBERS ARE SECONDARY AND CONTESTED — flagged as possibly fabricated by the audit; verify before budgeting or disqualifying.

A licence may be granted to an entity established or resident in another EU member state, but it MUST appoint a Slovak-seated registered representative — an establishment requirement that changes the entity structure, not just the paperwork. Models B and C: assume a licence is needed. Regulator: Urad pre regulaciu hazardnych hier (Gambling Regulatory Authority). VERIFICATION STATUS: act number reliable via CMS Expert Guide, section numbers UNVERIFIED.
subdivisions.authority: Act No. 30/2019 Coll. on gambling games. SECONDARY (CMS Expert Guide). SECTION NUMBERS UNVERIFIED.

subdivisions.detail: Loterija Slovenije and Sportna loterija retain the online monopoly for most verticals, so Model B cannot be licensed. Model C: no route identified; treat as closed. Regulator: Ministry of Finance / Financial Administration (FURS). VERIFICATION STATUS: directory- and guide-derived, no primary text checked.
subdivisions.authority: Gaming Act (Zakon o igrah na sreco, ZIS) — UNVERIFIED. Monopoly scope per EGBA analysis and CMS guide (SECONDARY).

subdivisions.name: Spain
subdivisions.detail: SKILL PREDOMINANCE IS NO DEFENCE ONCE A CHANCE ELEMENT IS PRESENT — WHICH IS NARROWER THAN 'NO PURE-SKILL EXEMPTION'. AUDIT CORRECTION: Art. 3(a) Ley 13/2011 defines 'juego' as any activity in which money or economically valuable objects are risked on uncertain future results 'DEPENDIENTES EN ALGUNA MEDIDA DEL AZAR' — dependent TO SOME DEGREE ON CHANCE — permitting transfer between participants, 'con independencia de que predomine en ellos el grado de habilidad, destreza o pericia de los jugadores o sean exclusiva o primordialmente de suerte, envite o azar'. The 'independencia de que predomine la habilidad' clause means skill-predominance is no defence once chance is present; it does NOT capture a contest with no chance element at all. The uncorrected brief's flat 'Spain expressly has NO pure-skill exemption' overstated this. For FACT//DUEL the practical answer is unchanged — the random question draw supplies the chance element — but the reasoning must be stated correctly. SECOND AUDIT CORRECTION: THE GENERAL-LICENCE CATEGORIES (apuestas, rifas, concursos, otros juegos) SIT IN ARTICLE 10, NOT ARTICLE 9. 'Concursos' is defined at Art. 3(e) as offers made through media (TV, radio, internet) requiring an economic outlay with prizes determined by chance, competition or knowledge tests — WHETHER AN APP-BASED DUEL FITS THAT DEFINITION IS UNTESTED and is a specific question for Spanish counsel, which the uncorrected brief never asked. Art. 2.2 excludes only games or competitions 'de puro ocio, pasatiempo o recreo que constituyan usos sociales' with no economically evaluable transfers, and excludes promotional combinations with random elements. A general licence must be held before the matching singular licence can be sought; general licences are awarded through a public convocatoria, not on demand. AUDIT ADDITIONS: Real Decreto 958/2020 severely restricts gambling advertising; player-winnings withholding tax and gambling VAT treatment change prize-pool economics and require payout-layer product changes; player-fund segregation is a licence condition. ALL THREE UNVERIFIED AS TO DETAIL. The DGOJ was consulting on amendments to Ley 13/2011 as at July 2026 (SECONDARY). Fees and lead times UNVERIFIED. VERIFICATION STATUS: PRIMARY TEXT CHECKED (BOE consolidated text).
subdivisions.authority: Ley 13/2011, de 27 de mayo, de regulacion del juego, Arts. 1, 2, 3, 10 (BOE-A-2011-9280, consolidated text fetched 14 Sep 2026) — ARTICLE 10 CORRECTED FROM ARTICLE 9 PER AUDIT; Art. 3(e) 'concursos' definition added per audit. Real Decreto 1614/2011 on licences, authorisations and registers. Real Decreto 958/2020 (advertising) — UNVERIFIED. Regulator: Direccion General de Ordenacion del Juego (DGOJ).

subdivisions.name: Sweden
subdivisions.status: licence-required — REVERSED BY THE AUDIT from the uncorrected brief's 'outside gambling law'
subdivisions.detail: THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL SUBDIVISION REVERSAL IN THIS CORRECTED EDITION. The uncorrected brief placed Sweden in the 'outside gambling law, no licence' camp in its headline and Model C analysis, on the strength of a Spelinspektionen page about competitions decided by a prestationsmoment — while its own subdivision row simultaneously said 'licence-required'. A founder reading the headline would have launched paid contests in Sweden unlicensed. CORRECTED POSITION: Spellagen defines KOMBINATIONSSPEL as 'spel dar deltagarna har chans att vinna ett pris och dar sannolikheten att vinna beror pa en kombination av skicklighet och slump' — a game where participants have a chance to win a prize and the probability of winning depends on a COMBINATION OF SKILL AND CHANCE — and kombinationsspel is a licensable form of spel, structurally identical to the Danish kombinationsspil the brief already treated as fatal (definition verified against the Spellag text, 14 Sep 2026). The Spelinspektionen carve-out is strict on its own wording: it exempts only competitions where the winner is decided by a performance element 'UTAN INSLAG AV LOTTNING ELLER SLUMP' — WITHOUT any element of drawing lots or chance, not merely 'predominantly skill'. A randomly drawn question set introduces exactly the inslag av slump that defeats it. ON ITS OWN FACTS FACT//DUEL'S PAID DUEL IS A CANDIDATE SWEDISH KOMBINATIONSSPEL REQUIRING A SPELINSPEKTIONEN LICENCE. A Swedish Model C would need an identical fixed question set for every entrant, no random matching, and no chance-introducing timer — and even then a Swedish opinion. Other exemptions at 3 kap. 4-5 §§ Spellagen: FREE-TO-ENTER GAMES (3 kap. 4 § — 'licens kravs inte for spel dar deltagande inte kraver betalning av en insats'), private play between close connections, combination games in periodicals/radio/TV, and municipal non-profit lotteries. Model B requires a Spelinspektionen licence. AUDIT ADDITION: player-fund segregation is a Swedish licence condition — DETAIL UNVERIFIED. An amending act SFS 2025:767 exists and ITS CONTENT IS ENTIRELY UNVERIFIED — it could affect this position. Fees and lead times UNVERIFIED. VERIFICATION STATUS: PRIMARY TEXT CHECKED for the kombinationsspel definition and the no-stake exemption.
subdivisions.authority: Spellag (2018:1138), in force 1 January 2019 — kombinationsspel definition and 3 kap. 4-5 §§ exemptions, verified against the Spellag text 14 Sep 2026 (riksdagen.se / svenskforfattningssamling.se). Spelforordning (2018:1475). Spelinspektionen guidance page 'Nar kravs det inte licens?' fetched 14 Sep 2026 — NOTE the guidance is narrower than the uncorrected brief read it. SFS 2025:767 — CONTENT UNVERIFIED. Regulator: Spelinspektionen.

subdivisions.name: Sweden — CPC enforcement precedent
subdivisions.detail: The CPC Network's coordinated action announced alongside the Key Principles on 21 March 2025 targeted Star Stable Entertainment AB, a Swedish game operator, over direct exhortation to children in advertisements and time-limited pressure techniques in a virtual-currency economy. This is the live example of how the Key Principles are actually enforced — as a coordinated CPC action against a single operator, with commitments sought. Read it as the enforcement template for any coin economy aimed at or reaching minors. Note the enforcement value is independent of whether the Key Principles are binding: a CPC coordinated action is itself the punishment regardless of the eventual legal answer.
subdivisions.authority: CPC Network coordinated action, announced 21 March 2025 (European Commission news release)

checklist.item: Accept and design around the fact that there is no EU gambling licence and no mutual recognition — budget for per-member-state licensing, not one EU authorisation
checklist.issuer: European Commission (DG GROW) / CJEU
checklist.prerequisite: None
checklist.notes: The Commission's online gambling page states that there is no sector-specific EU legislation in the field of gambling services and that EU countries are autonomous in how they organise gambling services. CJEU Case C-440/23 — AUDIT FLAGGED THIS AS POSSIBLY FABRICATED; THE EDITOR CHECKED AND THE CASE IS REAL. It is European Lotto and Betting Ltd and Deutsche Lotto- und Sportwetten Ltd, judgment of 16 April 2026, following AG Emiliou's opinion of 4 September 2025 (CELEX 62023CC0440). Holdings as reported across GTG Advocates, Gecic Law, Mondaq, BSP and AGB: EU law does not preclude a member state prohibiting online gambling services authorised in another member state; member states may attach civil-law consequences including nullity of contracts and restitution of lost stakes; a player's restitution claim is not an abuse of EU rights. The underlying facts were Malta-licensed operators serving German players between June 2019 and July 2021. The judgment text itself was not fetched from curia.europa.eu — the holdings are corroborated across multiple independent practitioner sources but remain SECONDARY as to exact wording.

checklist.item: Decide the launch shape FIRST: Model A/D (no gambling licence anywhere) vs Model C (split 27 ways, and not where you thought) vs Model B (do not attempt in the EU)
checklist.issuer: Founder / board decision
checklist.prerequisite: None
checklist.notes: Recommended EU sequencing: ship Model A + Model D EU-wide now with zero gambling licensing (subject to the Model A conditions — no randomised paid rewards anywhere, Belgium especially); treat Model C as a licensed-market product state by state; drop Model B for the EU. CORRECTED: the sweepstakes structure fails in the EU not because 'no consideration gateway exists' (several states DO exempt genuinely free-to-enter games — Spellagen 3 kap. 4 § is explicit) but because no member state accepts a DUAL paid-plus-free entry route as cleansing the paid route, and France defeats it in terms via L320-1 CSI. A genuinely free-only product is a different and possibly viable design; a paid product with a free side door is not.

checklist.item: Geo-block France for any paid-entry contest or staking product, and geo-block it hard (IP + payment BIN + device)
checklist.issuer: ANJ (Autorite Nationale des Jeux)
checklist.prerequisite: Server-authoritative geolocation at account and transaction level
checklist.notes: CORRECTED RATIONALE. L320-1 CSI catches operations offered to the public to create the hope of a gain due EVEN PARTIALLY to chance where a financial sacrifice is required, and adds that the prohibition covers games whose operation rests on the players' savoir-faire. France therefore catches any paid contest with ANY chance element — it does NOT prohibit skill contests as a class (paid chess, bridge and quiz competitions continue lawfully). The geo-block conclusion is unchanged for FACT//DUEL because randomly drawn questions and reflex timers supply the chance element, but the reason matters: a fully deterministic, fixed-question, no-timer format is not automatically illegal in France and would need French counsel rather than a blanket assumption. The video-game competition carve-out at Arts. L321-8 to L321-11 CSI requires PHYSICAL PRESENCE of participants. ANJ licences exist only for sports betting, horse betting and online poker. L320-1 WORDING WAS NEVER FETCHED FROM LEGIFRANCE (403) BY EITHER THE RESEARCHER OR THE AUDITOR — confirm the consolidated wording with French counsel.

checklist.item: Geo-block or free-only in: Poland, Cyprus, Slovenia, Belgium, Austria (pending reform), Finland (until 1 July 2027) for any staking/prize product
checklist.issuer: MF Poland / National Betting Authority CY / FURS SI / Kansspelcommissie BE / BMF AT / National Police Board FI
checklist.prerequisite: Geolocation stack
checklist.notes: These are monopoly or closed-class markets where a P2P staking product cannot be licensed at all. AUSTRIA REFORM DETAILS ARE CONTESTED AND SHOULD NOT BE PLANNED AGAINST: the audit could not confirm the August 2026 Commission notification, the reported 20-30 licences, the 15 July 2026 consultation close, the 1 January 2027 exit deadline or the 18-month (rising to 24 from 2030) exclusion period. Verify against a TRIS notification number before any geo-block or exit decision rests on the 1 January 2027 date. The audit also notes that Oesterreichische Lotterien's existing electronic-lotteries concession has a fixed expiry which is what actually drives the reform timetable — that expiry date is UNVERIFIED. Finland: the new Gambling Act was approved by the President on 16 January 2026; applications opened 1 March 2026 and the licensed market goes live 1 July 2027 (valtioneuvosto.fi / intermin.fi — section numbers UNVERIFIED).

checklist.item: Establish the EU operating entity in Malta and apply to the MGA
checklist.issuer: Malta Gaming Authority (MGA); Gaming Act Cap. 583
checklist.leadTime: UNVERIFIED — consultancies quote 4-6 months for a clean application and 6-12 months for complex ownership or novel products; the MGA publishes no service-level commitment that could be verified. Treat consultancy figures as marketing material.
checklist.prerequisite: Maltese company, fit-and-proper relevant persons, business plan, system and game design documents
checklist.notes: CITATION CORRECTED: the governing instrument is the Gaming Act (Cap. 583), enacted by Act XVI of 2018, which replaced the Lotteries and Other Games Act (Cap. 438) and repealed its subsidiary legislation including the Skill Games Regulations S.L. 438.11. Do not cite S.L. 438.11. Fees verified from the MGA's 'Licence Fees and Taxation' guidance note, December 2024 v3, which cites Gaming Licence Fees Regulations S.L. 583.03 and Gaming Tax Regulations S.L. 583.10. AUDIT ADDITION: several regimes require an EEA-established entity with local tax registration before an application is even accepted, and some require a local presence or representative — Slovakia requires a Slovak-seated registered representative; Poland requires a Polish seat or office; equivalent requirements in Hungary, Czechia, Greece and Romania are UNVERIFIED but should be assumed.

checklist.item: Choose the MGA licence type: Type 4 (controlled skill game) if the MGA will classify a knowledge duel as one; Type 3 (P2P, operator takes commission) if it will not — AND UNDERSTAND THAT THIS CHOICE IS AN EU-WIDE CHARACTERISATION, NOT A FORM-FILLING DECISION
checklist.issuer: Malta Gaming Authority
checklist.cost: Fixed annual licence fee: EUR 10,000 if providing SOLELY Type 4 services; EUR 25,000 for a B2C Gaming Service Licence otherwise (incl. Type 3). Minimum share capital: Type 4 EUR 40,000, Type 3 EUR 40,000, Types 1-2 EUR 100,000
checklist.prerequisite: MGA application accepted; game design documentation demonstrating that skill determines the outcome alone or predominantly
checklist.notes: AUDIT CORRECTION — THE UNCORRECTED BRIEF RECOMMENDED TYPE 3 AS THE 'LIKELIER FIT' WITHOUT FLAGGING THE CONSEQUENCE. Type 3 is, on the MGA's own definition, a class of GAMES OF CHANCE ('games of chance not played against the house and wherein the operator is not exposed to gaming risk'). Applying for Type 3 concedes that the product is a game of chance — which destroys the skill-predominance argument in Germany and Austria, weakens it in the Netherlands, and strengthens capture in Denmark, Spain, Ireland, Sweden and Italy. Type 3 and Type 4 are NOT interchangeable fallbacks. If the EU strategy depends on Model C being outside gambling law anywhere, do not file for Type 3. Type 4 = controlled skill games. CRITICAL GAP (unchanged by the audit): under Directive 6 of 2018 (Controlled Skill Games Ruling, 1 August 2018) FANTASY SPORTS IS THE ONLY GAME THE MGA HAS CLASSIFIED as a controlled skill game; a trivia duel needs a fresh MGA determination, so budget for a pre-application ruling request. The burden of proving skill predominance is on the applicant. The reg. 8 Gaming Authorisations Regulations cross-reference could not be verified against primary text by either the researcher or the auditor; the auditor notes the Gaming Authorisations Regulations are S.L. 583.05 — REGULATION NUMBER UNVERIFIED.

checklist.item: Budget the MGA compliance contribution and the new Maltese gaming tax — AND RE-RUN THE ECONOMICS FOR THE NEW TAXABILITY TEST
checklist.issuer: MGA / Commissioner for Revenue, Malta
checklist.cost: Type 4 compliance contribution: minimum EUR 5,000, maximum EUR 500,000 per year; rates 0.50% on first EUR 2m of gaming revenue, 0.75% on next EUR 3m, 1.00% on next EUR 5m, 1.25% on next EUR 5m, 1.50% on next EUR 5m, 1.75% on next EUR 10m, 2.00% on remainder. Type 3: minimum EUR 25,000, maximum EUR 500,000; 4.00% on first EUR 2m tapering to 0.40%. Gaming tax: from 1 October 2026 the single 5% rate is replaced by 15% of aggregate gaming revenue for Type 1 and 10% for Types 2, 3 and 4 (5% retained for controlled gaming premises and junkets).
checklist.leadTime: Payable monthly, by the 20th of the month following the reference month. The tax change TAKES EFFECT 1 OCTOBER 2026 — that is IN THE FUTURE as at the date of this correction (14 September 2026).
checklist.prerequisite: Licence issued
checklist.notes: Compliance contribution figures verified from the MGA guidance note (Dec 2024 v3). GAMING TAX: the audit flagged this as possibly fabricated; THE EDITOR CHECKED AND IT IS REAL — PwC Malta ('Changes in Gaming Tax applicable from October 2026'), the MGA's own 'Enhancements to Malta's VAT and Gaming Tax Frameworks' announcement and an MTCA government press release all confirm the Gaming Tax (Amendment) Regulations 2026 coming into force 1 October 2026, with 15% for Type 1 and 10% for Types 2-4. THE EXACT LEGAL NOTICE NUMBERS (reported as LN 84/2026 and LN 86/2026) REMAIN UNVERIFIED — do not cite them. MATERIAL FACT THE UNCORRECTED BRIEF MISSED ENTIRELY: for distance gaming the taxability test is being changed from the player's PHYSICAL PRESENCE in Malta to whether the player is established, has a permanent address and/or usually resides in Malta. The old 'only players physically in Malta' rule of thumb no longer states the rule and the base may be wider for a consumer app with Maltese-resident users. The device-based levy is abolished and a higher fixed studio broadcasting levy introduced. A separate VAT change also takes effect 1 October 2026 — OUT OF LANE, UNANALYSED. Start-ups qualifying under the MGA's Start-Up Undertakings Directive get a 12-month compliance-contribution moratorium.

checklist.item: DO NOT run Model C in Germany unlicensed on the skill-predominance analysis alone — get a German opinion that covers BOTH § 3(1) GlueStV AND § 33d GewO
checklist.issuer: Gemeinsame Gluecksspielbehoerde der Laender (GGL), Halle (Saale), for GlueStV permissions; the competent Land/municipal trade authority (Gewerbebehoerde) for a § 33d GewO Erlaubnis
checklist.cost: UNVERIFIED for both the GGL permission and the § 33d GewO Erlaubnis
checklist.prerequisite: German legal opinion on (a) whether chance predominates in your specific duel format and (b) whether § 33d GewO applies to a purely online offering
checklist.notes: THIS ITEM IS THE MOST CHANGED IN THE DOCUMENT. The uncorrected brief's advice was 'run Model C in Germany unlicensed'. That advice is WITHDRAWN. CORRECTED PICTURE: (1) GlueStV 2021 permission classes are NOT limited to sports betting (§ 21), online poker (§ 22b), virtual slot machines (§ 22a), lotteries and horse betting — the GGL's own legal-basis page states GlueStV 2021 made licensable virtuelle Automatenspiele, Online-Poker UND ONLINECASINOSPIELE, and online casino games are authorised by the individual LAENDER under their own concession procedures, not by the GGL. There is still no class that fits a P2P knowledge stake, so Model B cannot be licensed in its current shape, but the word 'unlicensable' was overstated — restructuring into a licensable class is not categorically foreclosed. (2) Model C that escapes § 3(1) GlueStV does NOT thereby escape German permission requirements: § 33d GewO requires an Erlaubnis for the commercial operation of 'andere Spiele mit Gewinnmoeglichkeit' — other games with a chance to win that are not Gluecksspiel — with a Bundeskriminalamt Unbedenklichkeitsbescheinigung as a precondition and refusal mandated where the applicant lacks reliability (provision verified at gesetze-im-internet.de, 14 Sep 2026). ITS APPLICATION TO PURELY ONLINE OFFERINGS IS CONTESTED and is the exact question the German opinion must answer. (3) GET THE OPINION ON THE 5/7/10-SECOND TIMER AND THE RANDOM QUESTION DRAW before relying on the skill analysis at all. Statutory evaluation of GlueStV 2021 is due by 31 December 2026 under § 32 (section number SECONDARY); a successor treaty would not take effect before 2027-2028 (SECONDARY, trade press). No 2025 or 2026 amendment to GlueStV 2021 appears on the GGL's legal-basis page.

checklist.item: Apply for a Spanish DGOJ general licence in the 'concursos' (or 'otros juegos') category plus the matching singular licence
checklist.issuer: Direccion General de Ordenacion del Juego (DGOJ), Spain
checklist.leadTime: UNVERIFIED — general licences are granted through a public convocatoria, not on demand; timing depends on the DGOJ opening a round
checklist.prerequisite: General licence must be held before the corresponding singular licence can be requested
checklist.notes: CORRECTED ON TWO POINTS. (1) The uncorrected brief said 'Spain expressly has NO pure-skill exemption'. That overstates Art. 3(a) Ley 13/2011, which requires the uncertain future results to be 'dependientes EN ALGUNA MEDIDA DEL AZAR' — dependent to some degree on chance. The 'con independencia de que predomine... el grado de habilidad' clause means skill-predominance is no defence ONCE A CHANCE ELEMENT IS PRESENT; it does not capture a contest with no chance element at all. For FACT//DUEL the practical answer is the same (random question draw supplies the chance element) but the reasoning must be stated correctly. (2) THE GENERAL-LICENCE CATEGORIES (apuestas, rifas, concursos, otros juegos) SIT IN ARTICLE 10, NOT ARTICLE 9 — the uncorrected brief's authority line was wrong. 'Concursos' is defined at Art. 3(e) as offers made through media (TV/radio/internet) requiring an economic outlay with prizes determined by chance, competition or knowledge tests; WHETHER AN APP-BASED DUEL FITS THAT DEFINITION IS UNTESTED AND UNVERIFIED and is a specific question for Spanish counsel. Art. 2.2 excludes only games of puro ocio, pasatiempo o recreo constituting usos sociales with no economically evaluable transfers. AUDIT ADDITION: Spain's Real Decreto 958/2020 imposes severe gambling advertising restrictions, and player-winnings withholding tax and gambling VAT treatment change prize-pool economics — both UNVERIFIED as to detail and both capable of making a licensed Spanish product unmarketable. The DGOJ was consulting on Ley 13/2011 amendments as at July 2026 — SECONDARY.

checklist.item: Apply for an ADM concession in Italy if you want Italian players in any paid contest — but price the concession before planning on it
checklist.issuer: Agenzia delle Dogane e dei Monopoli (ADM), Italy
checklist.cost: NOT 'UNVERIFIED' IN THE SENSE OF UNKNOWN-BUT-SMALL. AUDIT ADDITION: D.Lgs. 41/2024 sets a multi-million-euro fee per remote concession, widely reported at around EUR 7m for a nine-year concession — FIGURE UNVERIFIED but the order of magnitude is the decision-relevant fact. Treat Italy as out of reach for an early-stage product until this is confirmed.
checklist.leadTime: UNVERIFIED — the 2024-25 reordering tender is closed. Reports that ADM awarded 52 concessions to 46 operators in September 2025 with each operator capped at 5 concessions are SECONDARY AND UNVERIFIED (the auditor could not confirm the counts).
checklist.prerequisite: Wait for or qualify under a future ADM bando
checklist.notes: Italy explicitly regulates skill games with cash prizes rather than exempting them: D.M. 17 settembre 2007 n. 186, 'Regolamento per la disciplina dei giochi di abilita a distanza con vincita in denaro', covers games where the result depends PREDOMINANTLY OVER the random element on player skill — so demonstrating skill predominance in Italy puts you INSIDE the licensing regime, not outside it. The remote sector was reordered by D.Lgs. 25 marzo 2024 n. 41, in force 4 April 2024. AUDIT ADDITION — ADVERTISING: Italy operates a near-total gambling advertising ban under the Decreto Dignita. A licensed Model C in Italy could be legal to operate and impossible to market. For a consumer app that is decisive, and it was entirely absent from the uncorrected brief.

checklist.item: Apply for a Dutch KSA remote gambling licence if you want Model B; Model C MAY fall outside the Wok but the appellate weather is against you
checklist.issuer: Kansspelautoriteit (KSA), Netherlands
checklist.prerequisite: Dutch legal opinion on 'overwegende invloed'
checklist.notes: CORRECTED. Wok Art. 1(1)(a): gambling exists where winners are determined by a chance mechanism on which participants cannot generally exert decisive influence ('overwegende invloed'); a genuine behendigheidsspel falls outside. The uncorrected brief presented this as a live 50/50 by citing a 2010 Hague District Court decision against the 1998 Hoge Raad poker ruling. AUDIT CORRECTION: the 2010 decision was REVERSED ON APPEAL by the Gerechtshof Den Haag and Dutch higher courts have consistently held poker to be a kansspel. The test has been applied AGAINST skill claims at appellate level. The Netherlands is materially less favourable for Model C than the uncorrected brief implied. Wok statutory text was never fetched (SECONDARY). Current licensing: new policy rules BVRKOA 2026 in force 1 January 2026; the September 2021 cohort of licences EXPIRES 1 OCTOBER 2026 (a FUTURE event as at 14 September 2026 — the uncorrected brief's risks section stated this in the completed past tense); licences run a maximum of 5 years; applicants must file an exit plan and a change-notification plan. The KSA's 2026 Toezichtagenda prioritises illegal supply through an alliance with payment providers, social media and hosting parties. AUDIT ADDITION: the Dutch Gedragscode promotionele kansspelen governs promotional games that sit outside the Wok, and the Netherlands operates an untargeted-gambling-advertising ban — UNVERIFIED as to detail.

checklist.item: Track the Irish GRAI remote gaming licence window and apply when it opens — but treat every Irish date in this document as provisional
checklist.issuer: Gambling Regulatory Authority of Ireland (GRAI)
checklist.cost: UNVERIFIED — the Gambling Regulation Act 2024 leaves fees to be prescribed by the GRAI with the Minister's consent, so NO FEE FIGURE SHOULD BE BUDGETED. The pre-existing remote bookmaker regime's EUR 10,000 fee and EUR 10,000-200,000 biennial renewals are SECONDARY and are not the new regime's fees.
checklist.prerequisite: Irish or in-scope entity; fit-and-proper declarations for every relevant officer and beneficial owner; tax clearance
checklist.notes: Ireland matters because its definition of gaming expressly catches skill: 'games of skill or chance (or partly of skill and partly of chance) where the participant pays money for the chance to win a prize of money (or money's worth)'. CONTESTED / PROVISIONAL PER AUDIT: none of the commencement dates or exemption thresholds could be verified by either the researcher or the auditor — irishstatutebook.ie, oireachtas.ie and grai.ie all returned 403. The reported timeline (commencement order signed 3 February 2026, effective 5 February 2026; remote betting applications opened 9 February 2026; remote betting licence requirement from 1 July 2026; in-person from 1 December 2026) and the reported exemption thresholds (one-off charitable lotteries under EUR 2,000; marketing lotteries capped at EUR 5,000) are ALL UNVERIFIED — the betting dates are corroborated across DLA Piper, LexisNexis and gov.ie, which is better than nothing but is still secondary. The s. 2 definitions on which the whole Irish verdict turns are quoted only through a law-firm guide. REMOTE GAMING (B2C) LICENCES ARE REPORTED AS NOT YET OPEN, variously Q4 2026 or 2027-28 — confirm directly with the GRAI Operator Portal before any Irish planning. Administrative sanctions are reported at up to EUR 20m or 10% of turnover (UNVERIFIED).

checklist.item: Apply for a Danish Spillemyndigheden licence for any paid contest with Danish players
checklist.issuer: Spillemyndigheden, Denmark
checklist.prerequisite: None identified
checklist.notes: Spilleloven § 5 defines 'kombinationsspil' as activities where the chance of winning depends on 'en kombination af faerdighed og tilfaeldighed' — skill AND chance combined — and these require a licence. Only games decided purely by skill fall outside the Act. A trivia duel with randomly drawn questions is a textbook kombinationsspil. Spillemyndigheden's public guidance: charge for participation and you need permission; make it free and you do not. Danish statutory text was fetched from danskelove.dk. NOTE THE READ-ACROSS THE UNCORRECTED BRIEF MISSED: Sweden has the structurally identical kombinationsspel concept, which is why Sweden has been moved out of the 'no licence' camp in this corrected edition.

checklist.item: Apply for a Spelinspektionen licence for any paid contest with Swedish players — SWEDEN IS A LICENCE MARKET FOR THIS PRODUCT, NOT AN EXEMPT ONE
checklist.issuer: Spelinspektionen, Sweden
checklist.prerequisite: Swedish legal opinion on whether the duel is a kombinationsspel
checklist.notes: AUDIT-DRIVEN REVERSAL — THIS ITEM REPLACES THE UNCORRECTED BRIEF'S PLACEMENT OF SWEDEN OUTSIDE GAMBLING LAW.
