EU AML Regulation (EU) 2024/1624: no article number, EUR customer-due-diligence threshold for gambling, member-state low-risk exemption, or date of application is asserted. eur-lex.europa.eu returned empty responses across four separate fetch attempts (HTML, PDF, CELEX and ELI URL forms) and the environment's proxy would not relay it. Everything about AMLR in this report is a statement of what counsel must find, not a finding.

India, Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act 2025: the section numbers (reported as sections 5, 6 and 7 for the offering, advertising and financial-transaction prohibitions), the penalty amounts (reported as up to 3 years imprisonment and INR 1 crore) and the commencement date all come from secondary sources — Trilegal, PIB press releases and Wikipedia. meity.gov.in and indiacode.nic.in both returned HTTP 403, and ogai.gov.in was refused by the proxy gateway. The substance — a total ban on online money games including skill games, plus a payment-facilitation prohibition — is corroborated across independent sources and is safe to plan around; the citations are not safe to file.

31 CFR 1010.311 and 1010.306 (Currency Transaction Report threshold and filing deadline) were not verified. ecfr.gov redirects to an unblock page from this environment. The $10,000 figure is well known but is not asserted here as verified, and CTR applicability to a card-funded online game is genuinely doubtful since CTRs attach to currency.

31 CFR 1010.100(ff)(8): the $1,000-per-person-per-day de minimis that applies to most MSB categories and its reported non-application to money transmitters could not be confirmed. The Cornell fetch did not surface it. If a money transmitter has no de minimis — which is the conventional understanding — then even a single small redeemable payout creates MSB status, which is a material planning fact. Confirm before relying on it.

The CSBS MTMA's definition of 'money' and the game-platform / merchant-rewards exclusion within its virtual-currency definition were confirmed only through secondary analyses of Virginia's enactment. The actual model-law text was not fetched. This is the single most valuable item to verify because it determines whether Model A needs any state licence at all.

UK Online Safety Act 2023: 'highly effective age assurance', the commencing duties, the in-force date and whether licensed gambling is carved out to the Gambling Commission's LCCP instead were all unverified — ofcom.org.uk returned HTTP 403. The commonly cited 25 July 2025 commencement for HEAA duties is not asserted here.

EU Digital Services Act Article 28 minor-protection duties and the Commission's 2025 guidelines on protection of minors were not researched at all; the web-search budget was exhausted before reaching them. Age assurance expectations in the EU are therefore a gap in this report.

Published per-verification pricing for Persona, Sumsub, Veriff, Onfido and Jumio could not be obtained from vendor sites — withpersona.com/pricing and veriff.com/product/pricing returned 403 and 404 respectively. The indicative $0.80-$5.00 range comes from low-quality SEO comparison blogs and should be treated as worthless for budgeting. Only Stripe Identity's $1.50 document-and-selfie and $0.50 ID-number-lookup prices were verified from stripe.com/pricing.

Apple's current commission rates (standard, Small Business Program, and the US external-purchase-link rate) and Google Play's base service fee were not verified; only Play's India/South Korea 4-percentage-point alternative-billing reduction was confirmed from the Payments policy.

Card-network treatment was not researched: MCC 7995 assignment rules, Visa's and Mastercard's high-integrity-risk or high-brand-risk merchant registration programmes, their registration fees and their required transaction-coding are all unverified. These are a real and significant cost line for Models B and C and need to come from the prospective acquirer.

Lead times and fees for state money transmitter licences, EMI authorisation, and gambling-specialist PSP onboarding are all UNVERIFIED. Historically a broad US MTL footprint is a multi-year, seven-figure programme, but no current figure is asserted.

Whether a Model C fixed-prize skill contest entry fee constitutes a 'wager' for IRS purposes — determining Form W-2G versus Form 1099-MISC Box 3 treatment — is unresolved. The Instructions for Forms W-2G and 5754 (rev. 01/2026) address gambling winnings only and are silent on skill contests. This needs a tax opinion, not a search result.
Texas v. New Jersey (1965) and the unclaimed-property priority rules were not verified in this research; the incorporation-state fallback is stated from general knowledge and flagged accordingly.

PSD3 and the Payment Services Regulation: the reported 27 November 2025 provisional political agreement, publication in the Official Journal in H1 2026, and application around 2027 are from a single secondary commercial source and were not corroborated against Council or Parliament materials.

RBI Payment Aggregator directions: the current merchant-onboarding rules and prohibited-category list were not fetched. Whether an Indian PA will onboard a non-redeemable in-game coin post-Act is an assumption, not a finding.

This is a compliance checklist assembled from public sources, not legal advice. Models B and C require licensed gambling/gaming counsel in each target jurisdiction plus US money-transmission counsel before any merchant application is filed. Model A needs a short opinion on the MTMA game-platform exclusion and on whether the coin is 'property' for escheatment. Model D needs only routine auto-renewal and consumer-law review.

AUDIT ADDITION — UIGEA and Regulation GG citations (31 U.S.C. 5361-5367; 12 CFR Part 233; 31 CFR Part 132; 18 November 2008 final rule) were established via web search against FDIC and Cornell LII materials, not fetched from eCFR, which remains blocked from this environment. The existence, effect and payment-processor reach of the statute are well corroborated; confirm the Part numbers and publication date before quoting them in a filing.

AUDIT ADDITION — the EU AMLR application date of 10 July 2027 is corroborated across several independent practitioner sources (Deloitte, Bird & Bird, EU AML-package readiness commentary) but was not fetched from EUR-Lex, which was unreachable across four attempts in the original research and was not retried. The reported first EU-level definition of 'gambling service' as covering games of chance 'including those with an element of skill', attributed in secondary sources to Article 2(1)(12), is UNVERIFIED as to both the article number and the wording, and is decision-critical for Model C. Counsel must read it from primary text.

AUDIT ADDITION — New York and Florida prize-promotion registration: the $5,000 aggregate-prize threshold, the 30-day (NY) and 7-day (FL) pre-opening deadlines, the bond-covers-total-advertised-value rule and the administering agencies all come from sweepstakes-practice law-firm commentary. No agency page or statute was fetched. Treat every figure as indicative and confirm with sweepstakes counsel.

AUDIT ADDITION — whether any licence exists for a pure paid-entry skill contest in the UK or in specific EU member states. The UK position (lawful without a Gambling Commission licence where skill genuinely determines the outcome) is from practitioner commentary on the Gambling Act 2005, not from Commission primary guidance, and no EU member-state position was checked. This single question determines whether Adyen's waiver prerequisite for Model C is satisfiable at all, and therefore whether Model C has any mainstream EU rail.

AUDIT ADDITION — Apple's Small Business Program terms (15% up to USD 1,000,000 of prior-calendar-year proceeds, 30% standard) are well corroborated across 2026 practitioner summaries and Apple's own SBP page was identified but not fetched in this pass. The reported EU DMA alternative-business-terms rate of 13% and any current US external-purchase-link commission rate are UNVERIFIED and in active litigation flux. Google Play's base service fee was not verified at all; only the India / South Korea 4-percentage-point alternative-billing reduction is confirmed from the Payments policy.

AUDIT ADDITION — Visa Dispute Monitoring Program and Mastercard Excessive Chargeback Program thresholds, ratios, fine schedules and remediation timelines were not researched. For a digital-goods merchant these are a live operational constraint on Model A and need to come from the prospective acquirer.

AUDIT ADDITION — the PCI SSC FAQ points relied on here (that a processor attestation is an alternative to deploying 6.4.3/11.6.1 techniques yourself, and that the new SAQ A criteria apply only to embedded-iframe merchants so a full redirect is out of scope) were established by the auditor, not fetched in this pass. Confirm both with your QSA or acquirer before designing the checkout around them.

AUDIT NOTE on the India Act — the Act number, assent date and Rules-notification date previously asserted are withdrawn because their source carried an AI-generated-content warning. Commencement status (reported as not yet in force) and the pending High Court and Supreme Court challenges are also UNVERIFIED. The prohibition's substance and its payment-facilitation limb remain corroborated across independent law-firm sources and are safe to plan around; none of the specific citations is safe to file.

AUDIT NOTE on Stripe — the phrase 'regardless of local legality' is withdrawn as a quotation; it could not be confirmed as text on Stripe's prohibited-business FAQ. The substance (local legality does not by itself make the category acceptable, because Stripe's own processor and financial-partner obligations bind) is sound and is retained unquoted. The adjacent phrase 'games of skill (or chance) with cash prizes, sweepstakes, pay-in auctions' IS verbatim and may be quoted.

AUDIT NOTE on Apple Guideline history — the brief's warning about a 'historic Guideline 4.7.1 real-money-gaming restriction' that has since been removed could not be corroborated; Apple's real-money gaming and sweepstakes rules appear to have lived at 5.3 throughout. Current 4.7 covers mini apps, mini games, streaming games, chatbots, plug-ins and emulators, and current 4.7.1 concerns privacy, moderation and Guideline 3.1 conformity. Do not repeat the claimed citation history to counsel.
